## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

### Claims

**c1** (37:99): Ibrahim said that he was going to his Lord, who would guide him.

**c2** (37:100): He asked his Lord to grant him one of the righteous.

**c3** (37:101): God gave him glad tidings of a forbearing boy.

**c4** (37:102): When the boy reached the stage of striving along with him, Ibrahim told him that he saw in sleep that he was slaughtering him, and asked him to consider what he thought.

**c5** (37:102): The son answered that his father should do what he was commanded, and that, if God willed, he would find him among the patient.

**c6** (37:103-104): When both of them had submitted, and he had laid him down, God called to him.

**c7** (37:105): God said that Ibrahim had fulfilled the vision, and that in this way He rewards the doers of good.

**c8** (37:106): God says that this was the clear trial.

**c9** (37:107): God ransomed him with a great sacrifice.

**c10** (37:108-109): God left on him a mention among later generations: peace be upon Ibrahim.

**c11** (37:110-111): In this way God rewards the doers of good; Ibrahim was one of His believing servants.

### One-minute summary

Ibrahim saw in sleep that he was slaughtering his son, and told him so [c4]. The son told him to do as he was commanded, and God called to Ibrahim that he had fulfilled the vision and ransomed his son with a great sacrifice [c5][c7][c9].

### Complete story

Ibrahim said that he was going to his Lord, who would guide him, and he asked his Lord to grant him one of the righteous [c1][c2]. God gave him glad tidings of a forbearing boy [c3].

When the boy reached the stage of striving along with him, Ibrahim told him that he saw in sleep that he was slaughtering him, and asked what he thought [c4]. The son answered that his father should do what he was commanded, and that, if God willed, he would find him among the patient [c5].

When both of them had submitted, and he had laid him down, God called to him [c6]. God said that Ibrahim had fulfilled the vision, and that in this way He rewards the doers of good [c7]. God says that this was the clear trial [c8], and He ransomed him with a great sacrifice [c9]. God left on him a mention among later generations: peace be upon Ibrahim [c10]. He was one of God's believing servants [c11].

### Deep study

The passage runs from Ibrahim's prayer for a righteous child [c1][c2] and the glad tidings [c3] to the vision [c4], the answer [c5], the call [c6][c7] and the ransom [c9]. God names the event a clear trial [c8], and the passage closes with a mention left among later generations and a statement of reward [c10][c11]. The text speaks of the son and the vision throughout and does not give the son's name [c4][c5].

### Kids mode

Ibrahim saw in a dream that he was to sacrifice his son, and he told him [c4]. His son said to do what he was told, and that he would be patient [c5]. God called out to Ibrahim and ransomed his son [c7][c9].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage stresses submission on both sides: Ibrahim consults his son and the son answers with patience [c4][c5]. Another is that God names the event a trial and a reward for the doers of good [c7][c8].

### What the sources do not establish

- The verses do not name the son. Interpreters have identified him in different ways, and a scholar must decide how the page treats the question; this draft does not name him.
- Not established: the place, the time or the age of the son; the Arabic says only that he reached the stage of striving along with his father.
- The pronoun in 'ransomed him' (37:107) is not marked in the Arabic; it is generally read as the son, and a scholar should confirm the wording.
- The verse does not say how the great sacrifice was provided or what it was.
- Not established: whether the vision was repeated; the verse says only that Ibrahim saw it in sleep.
- The passage continues in 37:112-113 with a further glad tidings; those verses are outside this chapter and a scholar should decide whether to add them and how to word their relation to the boy of 37:101.
